question: How is radiation different from conduction and convection?

options.A: It happens much slower than other methods
options.B: It only occurs in liquids and gases
options.C: It needs no physical medium to transfer heat
options.D: It requires direct contact between objects

explanation: Radiation travels through space using electromagnetic waves without needing any physical contact or intervening matter. [learn more](BMP112_U4_T3#BMP112_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why does a baby warm up under a radiant heater without touching it?

options.A: The air around the baby is heated by convection currents
options.B: The mattress conducts heat upward into the infant's body
options.C: Electromagnetic waves transfer heat directly through space
options.D: Cool air rises and draws warm air down to the skin

explanation: Radiant warmers use infrared waves to transfer thermal energy across open space straight to the baby's skin. [learn more](BMP112_U4_T3#BMP112_U4_T3_h1)

question: Which part of the electromagnetic spectrum carries most thermal radiation?
explanation: Most thermal energy emitted by everyday objects and human bodies travels as invisible infrared waves. [learn more](BMP112_U4_T3#BMP112_U4_T3_h2)

question: What happens to thermal wave emission when an object's temperature increases?

options.A: It stops emitting waves and starts conducting heat
options.B: It changes its emission to ultraviolet light only
options.C: It emits shorter wavelengths with more energy
options.D: It produces longer wavelengths with less total power

explanation: As objects get hotter, they radiate energy at higher intensities and shift toward shorter wavelengths on the spectrum. [learn more](BMP112_U4_T3#BMP112_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is a cold radiant sink in a clinical setting?

options.A: A cold surrounding surface that absorbs patient body heat
options.B: A wet floor that cools the room through evaporation
options.C: An air conditioner blowing freezing air onto the bed
options.D: A metal instrument tray that conducts cold into tissue

explanation: Cold walls, windows, and large equipment act as radiant sinks, pulling heat away from the warmer patient body. [learn more](BMP112_U4_T3#BMP112_U4_T3_h3)

question: A patient in a warm delivery room still feels chilled because the exterior window is very cold. What is causing this heat loss?

options.A: Direct conduction of heat through the open ward air
options.B: Net radiative heat loss to the cold window surface
options.C: Rapid evaporation of sweat from the skin surface
options.D: Convective drafts circulating around the room corners

explanation: Even in warm air, the body loses heat via radiation if nearby solid surfaces have a much lower temperature. [learn more](BMP112_U4_T3#BMP112_U4_T3_h3)

question: Which type of surface is the best absorber of thermal radiation?
explanation: Dark, dull surfaces absorb and emit thermal radiation much more effectively than shiny or light-colored surfaces. [learn more](BMP112_U4_T3#BMP112_U4_T3_h4)

question: How does human skin absorb infrared radiation?

options.A: It repels thermal waves unless the room is freezing
options.B: It reflects all radiant heat if the skin is dark
options.C: It only absorbs radiation if coated in oil or cream
options.D: It absorbs infrared heat well regardless of skin color

explanation: Human skin absorbs infrared radiation effectively, meaning its absorption rate is high across all individuals. [learn more](BMP112_U4_T3#BMP112_U4_T3_h4)

question: Which newborn group is at the greatest risk of rapid radiative heat loss?

options.A: Healthy toddlers with high subcutaneous fat stores
options.B: Infants born in tropical climates during the afternoon
options.C: Premature infants with a high surface-area-to-mass ratio
options.D: Term babies wrapped tightly in several layers of cotton

explanation: Babies with a large surface area compared to their small body mass lose heat much faster to their surroundings. [learn more](BMP112_U4_T3#BMP112_U4_T3_h5)

question: Why is a foil space blanket effective at keeping a patient warm in a cold room?

options.A: It stops all conduction by blocking air movement completely
options.B: It reflects radiant heat back toward the patient's body
options.C: It absorbs cold air before it reaches the patient
options.D: It generates chemical heat when it touches human skin

explanation: Shiny metallic blankets reflect escaping infrared radiation back toward the patient, cutting down radiant heat loss. [learn more](BMP112_U4_T3#BMP112_U4_T3_h5)
